title: Business Requirements Document — Hospital Management System

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: The Hospital Management System (HMS) is designed to provide a centralized platform for managing comprehensive hospital operations. The strategic rationale for this system is to streamline and digitize critical workflows, including patient information management, medical records, appointments, staff management, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. By integrating these functions into a single platform, the hospital aims to improve operational efficiency, enhance patient care through accessible medical history, and ensure strict compliance with healthcare data privacy standards. The system will support role-based access for various hospital personnel and patients, ensuring that sensitive medical information is handled securely and efficiently.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body: The primary business objectives are to centralize hospital operations, improve patient experience through a dedicated portal, and ensure secure, auditable management of medical and financial data. Success metrics will be derived from the operational efficiency of the core workflows (e.g., patient registration to billing, admission to discharge) and the system's ability to maintain high availability and fast API responses. Specific quantitative metrics for response times and availability are currently open items requiring stakeholder input, as the source document specifies 'fast' and 'high availability' without defined numerical benchmarks.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body: In Scope: The system will cover patient registration and profile management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, OPD/IPD management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records (EMR), diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward management, billing and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff management, and inventory/procurement. It will also include a patient portal for viewing appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history, and doctor dashboards for clinical management. Out of Scope: The source document does not explicitly define out-of-scope items. However, it is implied that the system is focused on internal hospital operations and patient-facing services, and does not cover external third-party integrations beyond standard REST APIs unless specified in future iterations.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body: The key stakeholders and governance personas identified in the system are: Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient. Each persona will have role-based access to specific modules and functionalities. For example, Doctors will have access to dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes, while Patients will have access to a portal for viewing their own medical information. The Admin will oversee the entire system, including staff management and system configuration.

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: System must allow registration of patients and management of their profiles, including medical history, allergies, and vital signs.
Patient can be registered with all required fields; profile can be updated and viewed by authorized roles.
System must support scheduling of appointments and managing queues for OPD/IPD.
Appointments can be scheduled, rescheduled, and cancelled; queues are updated in real-time.
System must maintain comprehensive EMR including diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, and nursing notes.
EMR is accessible to authorized roles; all entries are timestamped and auditable.
System must allow lab technicians to process test requests and generate reports.
Test requests can be created, processed, and reports can be viewed by doctors and patients.
System must manage pharmacy prescriptions and track medicine inventory.
Prescriptions can be generated; inventory levels are updated upon dispensing.
System must handle billing, payments, insurance management, and generate invoices and receipts.
Bills are generated accurately; payments can be recorded; insurance claims can be processed.
System must provide a portal for patients to view appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history.
Patients can log in and view their own data; data is filtered to show only patient-specific information.
System must provide dashboards for doctors to manage appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes.
Doctors can view and update patient records; dashboards display relevant clinical information.
System must enforce role-based access for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient.
Users can only access modules and data relevant to their role; unauthorized access is denied.
System must maintain audit logs, ensure data validation, and implement security measures including encryption and secure authentication.
All critical actions are logged; data is encrypted at rest and in transit; authentication is secure.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body: Assumptions: The system will be deployed in a cloud or on-premise environment, using a suitable architecture with React/Next.js for frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, and Redis for caching/queues. Operational Constraints: The system must support responsive web UI, scalability, high availability, and fast API responses. It must also ensure secure authentication, password encryption, session management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error handling, logging, and regular backups. Specific numerical benchmarks for performance and availability are not provided in the source document and are open items requiring stakeholder input.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body: The system must comply with HIPAA and GDPR (if EU patients are involved) to ensure the privacy and security of medical information. It must also adhere to HL7 FHIR and DICOM standards for interoperability with other healthcare systems. The compliance baseline includes PHI encryption at rest (AES-256), audit trail immutability, and RTO < 1h / RPO < 5min. The source document specifies the need for security, audit logs, and privacy of medical information, which aligns with these compliance frameworks. However, specific implementation details for meeting these standards are not provided and are open items requiring stakeholder input.

Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
